topics.description: This is the Alpujarra–Sierra Nevada Almeriense local strategy for the 2023–2027 programme period, using the 544-page version 1 linked by the GDR and matched byte-for-byte to the existing library edition on 11 November 2026. It identifies cultural and natural rural heritage through a territorial diagnosis, local asset inventories and priorities. Section 3.4.1.10 distinguishes immovable, movable and intangible cultural heritage and cultural landscapes. NPL3 concerns conservation, enhancement and dissemination of cultural/natural heritage; OE3.3 tracks cultural and natural operations separately. Open the named landscapes and living-practice examples for concrete local evidence. Its intervention logic connects soil regeneration and erosion/aridity reduction to the heritage objective. This is documentary identification and strategic alignment, not an award, site-specific designation or automatic eligibility. The general legal definition and the applicable 2026 operation/selection rules remain separate. Version 1 is the currently linked edition checked here; later amendments are not assumed absent.

topics.description: This is the earlier Alpujarra–Sierra Nevada Almeriense strategy, titled Seguimos haciendo futuro, for the 2014–2020 programme. Its version 5 was adopted by the association’s extraordinary general assembly on 2 November 2023, as stated at PDF position 2; this records association adoption, not a separate claimed Junta approval. The historical diagnosis distinguishes cultural heritage, cultural landscapes and the natural-heritage system. Proyecto Programado 2 treats landscape as a fundamental heritage element, includes tangible and intangible assets, and discusses heritage infrastructure with or without formal designation, traditions, music, crafts and trovo. These passages show continuity in the local interpretation of rural heritage. They do not replace the current-period EDLL or the 2026 funding rules. Historical beneficiary classes, productive/nonproductive categories, percentages and caps retain their own programme and call context. Named sites and practices are documentary examples, not newly established awards or measured conservation outcomes.

topics.description: NPL3 is the current-period EDLL need for conservation, enhancement and dissemination of the area’s cultural and natural rural heritage by public and/or private entities. Its recorded prioritization value is 3.22. That number ranks a territorial need; it is not grant-selection points, a subsidy rate or a project score. The strategy’s intervention logic maps NPL3 to OE3.3 together with NPL4 soil regeneration/erosion/aridity and NPL8 climate action. The presence of private entities in this strategy need does not remove the applicant and nonproductive conditions of the particular operation type. Use the asset inventory and exact local priority as evidence, then check the separately applicable activity, applicant, cost and selection rules.

topics.description: OE3.3 is a strategic objective in the current-period EDLL: enhancement and dissemination of rural heritage. The strategy monitors cultural heritage through IN3.3.1 and natural heritage through IN3.3.2, with other indicators for participants, gender, climate and youth. The page 494 logic table maps NPL3 heritage, NPL4 soil regeneration and NPL8 climate action to this objective and lists operation types 3.1, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5. This documents strategic coherence rather than an approved application or a prescribed sequence of stages. The code OE3.3 is an objective identifier; operation type 3.3 is a different identifier for promotion, information and awareness.

topics.description: The current EDLL’s municipal inventory makes intangible heritage concrete. It lists pottery in Alhabia; barilla soap, artisan soap and barrel making in Terque; carpentry and glasswork in Alhama de Almería; viticulture, beehive making and named food preparations in Instinción; lace making, weaving and wine making in Ohanes; and viticulture in Padules. Festivals and other locally named traditions also appear in these rows. Section 3.4.1.10 explains the distinction between immovable, movable and intangible cultural heritage and cultural landscapes. These are source-listed practices and potential subjects for documenting cultural value. An inventory entry does not certify that every practitioner, event or modern commercial activity qualifies, or that any listed practice has received a grant. The activity’s heritage role and the proposed conservation/dissemination operation need their own evidence.

The descriptions document heritage characteristics; they do not establish a new conservation project, a funded intervention or current site condition.

topics.description: The 2014–2020 EDL version 5 uses a broad interpretation of rural heritage. Its cultural diagnosis distinguishes immovable architectural, ethnological and archaeological heritage, movable objects, intangible heritage and cultural landscapes. The strategy identifies cultural and natural heritage as complementary territorial resources. Proyecto Programado 2 treats landscape as fundamental and discusses conservation of heritage infrastructure with or without formal designation, together with recovery of traditions, music, crafts and trovo. It includes festivals or events that bring local historical or traditional values to public attention as possible operations in that former programme. These are historical strategy descriptions and proposed kinds of action, not proof that every example was funded, completed or successful. Their former applicant categories and aid limits do not transfer to today’s AL20 operation types.

topics.label: Patrimonio rural · rural heritage
topics.description: Rural heritage comprises the rural area’s architectural, historical, artistic, ethnological, ethnographic, cultural, environmental and landscape assets. It includes tangible and intangible heritage. For architectural/historical/artistic/ethnological/ethnographic/cultural assets, Article 3.5 points to official recognition or initiated recognition; a justified identification in the local strategy or an expert technical report can also establish rural-heritage status. A monument designation is therefore not the only evidential route, and private ownership or a rural location alone establishes neither qualification nor exclusion. Document what the asset is and why it matters. The child concepts explain cultural/documentary, living/intangible, environmental/geological, landscape and water/agricultural heritage. Their examples illustrate possible meanings, not automatic eligibility. 3.5 additionally requires the applicable public-interest, cost and dissemination/use conditions. The AL20 local layer is now available in separate Current EDLL 2023–2027 and Historical EDL 2014–2020 branches. The current EDLL explicitly combines cultural and natural heritage, identifies municipal living practices and four named cultural landscapes, and links NPL3 heritage with OE3.3. Its soil-regeneration correlation is strategic evidence, not an individual eligibility decision. The historical strategy separately explains landscapes, traditions, music, crafts and trovo. Keep legal recognition, justified local identification, priority/scoring and the eligibility of a proposed activity distinct.

topics.label: Living culture and intangible heritage
topics.description: Knowledge, oral traditions, music, skills and other intangible cultural assets can form rural heritage. The LEADER II trovo school teaches improvised oral poetry through historical discussion, recordings and practical games. The traditional-music festival is a separately documented cultural initiative. Training, awareness and conservation are different operation purposes; historical support does not make AL20 3.2 available. Current EDLL municipal tables supply concrete local practices such as Alhabia pottery, Terque soap/barrel making, Alhama carpentry/glasswork and Ohanes weaving/wine making. The historical EDL explicitly discusses recovery of music, traditions, crafts and trovo. A practice listed as intangible heritage is distinct from a grant-funded event or a particular practitioner’s commercial business.

topics.label: Landscape heritage
topics.description: Landscape can reflect interacting natural and human processes. Traditional settlement patterns, terraces, vegetation mosaics and rural views are illustrative investigation subjects, rather than a universal eligible list. Distinguish conserving the landscape’s documented value from commercial landscaping or simply improving private property. The source’s natural-heritage and landscape definitions support discussing ecological and cultural value together, while the funding operation still needs its own evidence. The current AL20 EDLL identifies Los Millares, agrarian Bentarique, viticultural Ohanes and the Sierra de Gádor mining landscape. Their descriptions give concrete archaeological, agrarian, water-system and industrial attributes. The historical EDL also treats landscape as fundamental heritage. These named cases give local documentary grounding beyond generic illustrative landscape examples.

topics.label: Water systems and agrarian heritage
topics.description: Historic irrigation channels, cisterns, mills, terraces, threshing floors and associated records or traditional knowledge can be investigated as cultural/landscape assets. These examples require documented heritage value. The Alcolea award explicitly concerns historical records of land allocation, water and acequias, compared with agricultural traditions. Category 3.5 excludes agricultural-production support; conservation of agrarian infrastructure is conditional on its final use not being agricultural production, processing or marketing. Restoring a working productive irrigation system is not automatically heritage funding. The current EDLL gives specific landscape evidence: Bentarique’s historic irrigation/orchard setting and Ohanes’s paratas, balates, acequias and viticultural knowledge. These descriptions establish why an agrarian water/landscape feature may have heritage value, while the quoted final-use restriction remains a separate current funding condition.

topics.label: Environmental and geological heritage
topics.description: Natural heritage includes biological and geological resources with relevant environmental, landscape, scientific or cultural value. The Spanish law distinguishes natural/seminatural habitats, species habitats, landscape and ecosystem restoration. Native habitats, ecological corridors, wetlands, significant trees or geological features are possible investigation subjects; a site assessment must establish the actual values and pressures. These are explanatory examples, not a designation of the user’s land or automatic LEADER eligibility. The AL20 EDLL explicitly includes natural heritage within NPL3 and assigns it a separate OE3.3 monitoring indicator. Its diagnostic response supports conservation and land-stewardship initiatives, and its intervention-logic table connects soil regeneration and erosion/aridity reduction to the heritage objective. These are source-stated strategic links; they do not classify every parcel or supply an approved restoration or planting plan.

topics.label: AL20 NPL4: soil regeneration, erosion and aridity
topics.description: NPL4 in the reviewed AL20 strategy calls for actions regenerating soils and reducing erosion and aridity, with a priority value of 3.16. It sits alongside NPL2 sustainable agriculture and NPL3 rural natural/cultural heritage. These are distinct strategic needs; their prioritization values do not award application points. The same strategy separately classifies broader natural-environment management measures under non-LEADER-addressable NPNL4. A restoration proposal therefore needs a justified mapping to the correct need, activity, applicant and funding rules rather than a blanket assumption that environmental work is eligible. The EDLL’s page 494 correlation table expressly places NPL4 beside NPL3 cultural/natural heritage and NPL8 climate action under OE3.3, listing operation types 3.1, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5. This supplies a documented route for explaining strategic coherence while preserving all separate eligibility and non-LEADER-management qualifications above.

topics.label: Enhancement of rural heritage
topics.description: Source criterion PT.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. PT.1.1: natural/monumental/architectural/artistic heritage enhanced for subsequent use through physical work, training, dissemination or awareness (13 points); PT.1.2: traditional trades/gastronomic specialties identified in EDLL (7); PT.1.3: other heritage action identified as of interest in EDLL (2). Family maximum 15. The September verification guide distinguishes proof at application from actual implementation at payment. PT.1.1 investments use a basic project for the intended heritage use; payment evidence can include execution project, final works certificate, reception record and photographs. For strategy-dependent .2/.3, the guide requires GDR justification and the latest applicable EDL. Annex VII marks PT.1 subcriteria cumulative, subject to the AL20 family maximum of 15. The EDLL itself also sets out PT.1 at position 449. Use the local heritage inventory to explain the specific asset or practice and retain the latest applicable selection/verification rules separately. NPL3’s priority value and OE3.3’s objective code are not additional PT.1 points.

findings.label: Los Millares · archaeological cultural landscape: documented heritage characteristics
findings.text: The EDLL reproduces an IAPH description of the Los Millares cultural landscape, identifying Santa Fe de Mondújar, Alhama de Almería and Gádor. It describes the settlement between the Andarax and Huéchar, fortifications, a collective necropolis and the interaction between archaeological remains and a semidesert natural setting. This is a landscape-scale cultural example, rather than only a single monument. The historical EDL also describes Los Millares and its cultural-landscape value. The descriptions document heritage characteristics; they do not establish a new conservation project, a funded intervention or current site condition.

findings.label: Bentarique · agrarian cultural landscape: documented heritage characteristics
findings.text: The current EDLL identifies Bentarique’s agrarian cultural landscape in the Andarax valley. Its reproduced IAPH account links orchard/fruit-growing land, the settlement and memory of Andalusi urbanism, historic irrigation, parrales and citrus, threshing floors and local agricultural traditions. This illustrates how land use, water systems, settlement and knowledge can form a heritage landscape. The earlier EDL also identifies the Bentarique landscape. The source’s historical and agrarian value is not a measured conservation outcome or an award. Heritage identification does not remove operation 3.5’s separate restrictions on agricultural-production support and the final use of agrarian infrastructure.

findings.label: Ohanes · viticultural cultural landscape: documented heritage characteristics
findings.text: The current EDLL describes Ohanes as a viticultural cultural landscape with terraces (paratas), dry-stone retaining walls (balates), irrigation channels (acequias), stone-working knowledge and the historic culture of the Ohanes/uva de barco grape. These interacting physical structures, land uses and inherited skills explain its landscape and cultural value. The historical EDL likewise discusses the terraced Ohanes landscape. This is a source-described heritage example; it does not establish a currently funded vineyard project, a validated restoration prescription or the condition of an individual parcel. A proposed heritage intervention must still meet applicable activity and agricultural-production exclusions.

findings.label: Sierra de Gádor · mining cultural landscape: documented heritage characteristics
findings.text: The current EDLL identifies the Sierra de Gádor mining cultural landscape in Berja. Its reproduced description explains extraction areas, workings and industrial remains from different periods, including galleries, ventilation shafts and hoisting/processing structures, and their relationship with the wider mountain landscape. It names the mining areas of Chirán and Castala and describes landscape traces of mining decline. This provides a documented industrial and cultural-landscape example. It is not a restoration specification, evidence that the remains are safe to visit, a grant award or a measured environmental outcome. Any conservation or public-interpretation proposal needs site-specific evidence and applicable rights and permissions.

findings.label: A justified EDL identification can support rural-heritage status
findings.text: Article 3.5 expressly includes a justified definition in an EDL, alongside the separate professional study/report route. The AL20 EDLL’s asset descriptions and cultural/natural interpretation can therefore supply relevant local heritage evidence. Identification of an asset, its relation to a strategy need, a selection criterion and the admissibility of the proposed activity are separate questions. No asset list or strategy alignment alone establishes an award or applicant eligibility.

findings.label: Current municipal inventory gives concrete intangible-heritage examples
findings.text: The current EDLL’s municipal inventory makes intangible heritage concrete. It lists pottery in Alhabia; barilla soap, artisan soap and barrel making in Terque; carpentry and glasswork in Alhama de Almería; viticulture, beehive making and named food preparations in Instinción; lace making, weaving and wine making in Ohanes; and viticulture in Padules. Festivals and other locally named traditions also appear in these rows. Section 3.4.1.10 explains the distinction between immovable, movable and intangible cultural heritage and cultural landscapes. These are source-listed practices and potential subjects for documenting cultural value. An inventory entry does not certify that every practitioner, event or modern commercial activity qualifies, or that any listed practice has received a grant. The activity’s heritage role and the proposed conservation/dissemination operation need their own evidence.

findings.label: The historical EDL explicitly includes landscape and living traditions
findings.text: The 2014–2020 EDL version 5 uses a broad interpretation of rural heritage. Its cultural diagnosis distinguishes immovable architectural, ethnological and archaeological heritage, movable objects, intangible heritage and cultural landscapes. The strategy identifies cultural and natural heritage as complementary territorial resources. Proyecto Programado 2 treats landscape as fundamental and discusses conservation of heritage infrastructure with or without formal designation, together with recovery of traditions, music, crafts and trovo. It includes festivals or events that bring local historical or traditional values to public attention as possible operations in that former programme. These are historical strategy descriptions and proposed kinds of action, not proof that every example was funded, completed or successful. Their former applicant categories and aid limits do not transfer to today’s AL20 operation types.

browse_groups.description: These four named cultural landscapes are identified in the current EDLL and described through IAPH material reproduced there: Los Millares, agrarian Bentarique, viticultural Ohanes and the Sierra de Gádor mining landscape. Open each asset for its characteristics, municipal setting and exact pages; the first three also have distinct historical EDL citations. They are documentary heritage examples, not a catalogue of grants or restoration projects. In particular, agrarian heritage value and the admissibility/final use of a proposed agricultural-water intervention are separate questions.

browse_groups.description: Read the prioritized need before considering the project-selection criterion. The strategy separates LEADER-addressable needs from other territorial needs and gives its own priority values. Water management and soil regeneration provide useful starting points. Its precision-agriculture innovation example names drones/sensors with municipal limits, while criterion evidence requires a justified match to the latest applicable local strategy. NPL3 cultural/natural heritage and objective OE3.3 are linked to the documented soil-regeneration correlation; priority values, objective identifiers and selection points remain distinct.
